```{r}
#| label: setup

pacman::p_load(here, tidyverse, palmerpenguins, treemapify)
```

## The question

**How many?**

Two charts that show the counts of a discrete variable: the pie plot and the treemap.

---

# 1. A pie plot {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**coord_polar()**

---

## One bar

```{r}
penguins |>
  count(species) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = "", y = n, fill = species)) +
  geom_col()
```

There is no `geom_pie()` in ggplot2. We start with one stacked bar. Each segment is one species.

---

## Pie

```{r}
penguins |>
  count(species) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = "", y = n, fill = species)) +
  geom_col(width = 1) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y")
```

`coord_polar(theta = "y")` bends the bar into a circle. `width = 1` closes the hole in the middle.

---

## Pie void

```{r}
penguins |>
  count(species) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = "", y = n, fill = species)) +
  geom_col(width = 1) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y") +
  theme_void()
```

`theme_void()` removes the axes. A pie has no use for them. Adelie has 152 penguins and Gentoo has 124, and the two slices look almost the same. A bar plot would show the difference at once.

---

# 2. A treemap {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**geom_treemap()**

---

A treemap draws one rectangle for each category. The area of the rectangle is proportional to the count. The `treemapify` package draws treemaps. `pacman::p_load(treemapify)` installs it on the first run.

---

## Treemap no label

```{r}
#| error: true
penguins |>
  count(species) |>
  ggplot(aes(area = n, fill = species)) +
  geom_treemap() +
  geom_treemap_text()
```

Read the error: `geom_treemap_text()` requires the missing aesthetic `label`. The text layer needs to know what to write.

---

## Treemap

```{r}
penguins |>
  count(species) |>
  ggplot(aes(area = n, fill = species, label = species)) +
  geom_treemap() +
  geom_treemap_text()
```

`label = species` writes the species name on each rectangle. Adelie and Gentoo differ visibly, and Chinstrap is the smallest.

---

# 3. Species inside each island {background-color="#1a5276" style="color: white;"}

**subgroup**

---

## Treemap subgroup

```{r}
penguins |>
  count(island, species) |>
  ggplot(aes(area = n, fill = species, label = species, subgroup = island)) +
  geom_treemap() +
  geom_treemap_subgroup_border() +
  geom_treemap_text(colour = "white") +
  geom_treemap_subgroup_text()
```

`subgroup = island` draws a border around each island. The species rectangles sit inside. Biscoe has Gentoo (124) and Adelie (44). Dream has Chinstrap (68) and Adelie (56). Torgersen has Adelie (52).

---

```{r}
  geom_treemap_subgroup_text()
```

Answer: [YOUR ANSWER HERE] has three rectangles. [YOUR ANSWER HERE] and [YOUR ANSWER HERE] have one rectangle each.

---

## Recap {.smaller}

| Task | Code |
|------|------|
| One stacked bar | `geom_col()` with `x = ""` |
| Bend the bar into a pie | `coord_polar(theta = "y")` |
| Remove the axes | `theme_void()` |
| Treemap rectangles | `geom_treemap()` with `aes(area = n)` |
| Text on the rectangles | `geom_treemap_text()` with `aes(label = species)` |
| Borders around groups | `aes(subgroup = island)` and `geom_treemap_subgroup_border()` |
